My final goal is to have Renjin integrated into Scala Spark SBT project and then reproduce the results from the following page:
http://www.lac.inpe.br/~rafael.santos/Docs/R/CAP386/IntroEDA-Iris.html

Here -> http://www.lac.inpe.br/~rafael.santos/cap386.html
he lists the following software required:

Create a free acount at GitHub <https://github.com/>.
Install R <https://cran.rstudio.com/> and RStudio <https://www.rstudio.com/>.
Install Anaconda <https://www.continuum.io/downloads>, also R Essentials <https://docs.continuum.io/anaconda/r_language> for Anaconda.
Install Docker <https://docs.docker.com/engine/installation/>, and the Jupyter Notebook Data Science Stack <https://github.com/jupyter/docker-stacks/tree/master/datascience-notebook>.
What do you think in terms of a reality check?

thanks
ilango

messages.body_plain:
It looks like this is an issue with SBT's HTTP client:
https://github.com/sbt/sbt/issues/3570

You can workaround this problem with SBT 1.1.x by using the command line
argument -Dsbt.gigahorse=false  or add the following to your build.sbt file:

updateOptions := updateOptions.value.withGigahorse(false)

I'm updating the docs to reflect this gotcha.

Regarding the example, you should be able to reproduce the results in Scala,
with the exception of the graphics, which Renjin doesn't currently support.

You won't need any of the additional software listed, SBT should pull in all
of Renjin's dependencies.

Best,
Alex

It looks like this is an issue with SBT's HTTP client:
https://github.com/sbt/sbt/issues/3570

You can workaround this problem with SBT 1.1.x by using the command line
argument -Dsbt.gigahorse=false

messages.body_plain:
Hi Sam,
I took a look at the maven plugin source, and it looks like it's only checking for C++ files that end in ".cpp".
I've just updated the list of extensions:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/2b9141a02b65c4d28189e3646ea04daf92025a5d

A new release should be availabe shortly.

For "vanilla" c++ code, this should be enough, though you may need to include a dependency on renjin's build of the standard c++library:
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
  <artifactId>libstdcxx</artifactId>
  <version>4.7.4-b19</version>
</dependency>

For further examples of builds, take a look at our fork of libxml2, which wraps an existing configure+make setup, providing the required compiler flags for GCC-Bridge, and then compiling the output of make+gcc into JVM bytecode.
https://github.com/bedatadriven/libxml2

The most customized build is probably that of libstdcxx itself, which uses gradle to download the GCC sources, compile a subset of sources using gcc directly, and then compile the intermediate results into JVM bytecode:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-libstdcxx/blob/master/gcc/build.gradle

Hope this helps,
Alex

Strangely enough, it wasn't our plugin at all, but a bug in GCC's debugging output:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/621e5a6cacc992f2255813f700e3035bed181f1d

We don't use this output any more, so I've just removed the -fdump-tree-gimple-verbose-raw-vops flag and the compilation completes now.

I see there is quite a bit more work ahead, however. Most of our work on GCC-Bridge has focused on compiling mathematical code, and I see this library relies heavily on the C++ standard library I/O.

This is actually something we're working on right now in order to better support Bioconductor file format packages, so fasttext will be another good test case for this effort.

I've done some work this evening fixing the way we link to global variables like cerr and cout, but I can't actually figure out where these variables are supposed to be initialized, so the main() routine of the library fails.

You might bump up your project to the latest version of Renjin and the latest build of renjin-libstdcxx (b27) and see if you can use the library via its API, if there is one.

I'll take another look in the coming days.

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
Dear Miguel,

I don't think that serializing an instance of RenjinScriptEngine, which includes a reference to an R Session, is possible, and probably not desirable. For example, if you open a file in an R session, read half, and then send the session to another computer over the wire, what would be a valid state for the session on the other end?

Rather than ship the whole session to the cluster, I'd suggest storing any state that you need as serializable java fields, and initialize a transient session only as needed for computation. Here is a super simple example:

class DistributionComputer implements Serializable {
// (serializable)
private double mean;

private transient RenjinScriptEngine scriptEngine;

public double[] compute() {
  if(scriptEngine == null) {
     // initialize scriptEngine
   }
   scriptEngine.put("mean", mean);
   return scriptEngine.eval("rnorm(n=100, mean = mean)").toDoubleArray();
}

}

(Not guaranteed to compile ;-)

Hope this helps,
Alex
